title: Patterning human kidney organoids with synthetic Wnt-secreting organizers.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file could be located, so none was opened. I checked: Europe PMC record (open access = No, not in PubMed Central, no supplementary files, no text-mined accessions); the science.org article page (HTTP 403, paywalled); the PubMed XML for PMID 42391378 (no DataBankList, i.e. no deposited-accession entry at all); NCBI GEO searches by author (Lindstrom NO = 35 series, Fausto CC = 8, Glykofrydis F = 1) and by topic (WNT9B/WNT11, 'Wnt-secreting organizers', 'axial nephron patterning', seqFISH+kidney) - none of the returned series matches this paper, the nearest are companion papers with different PMIDs (GSE293237/GSE283868/GSE283186, PMID 40855070; GSE264516 etc., PMID 40967224); NCBI BioProject search; Zenodo (0 hits), Dryad (0 hits), figshare (only unrelated hits); and the full text of the matching bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2024.11.30.626171, ~200,000 characters, read in two halves), which contains no Data Availability and no Code Availability statement and no accession number anywhere.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the content: that spatial transcriptomics (Xenium and seqFISH, named in the preprint) of developing human kidney at 13 and 16 weeks revealed a collecting-duct-adjacent-to-distant polarity across a WNT11/WNT9B boundary; that engineered WNT-secreting cells were added to organoids; that measurements included transcript distances from the collecting-duct surface for 9 collecting-duct tips, LEF1 protein gradients versus distance from the organizer, nephron volumes/areas and marker intensities; and that seven supplementary tables of differentially expressed genes exist. None of these numbers or files were seen by me.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. No downloadable data found anywhere. The Science article is paywalled (HTTP 403, Europe PMC open-access flag = No, no PubMed Central copy, no supplementary files). PubMed's record carries no deposited-accession entry. Author and keyword searches of GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus), BioProject, Zenodo, Dryad and figshare returned nothing matching this paper. The bioRxiv preprint's full text has no data- or code-availability statement and names no accession. This is not 'needs a login' - I could not establish that a public copy of the data exists at all.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not reached (stopped at A1), but noted for the record: the quantities the paper reports - distance from the collecting-duct surface, gradient steepness, nephron orientation angle toward the WNT source - are image-derived measurements that would have to be reconstructed from microscopy, not columns in a released table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not reached. No files, so no inputs verified.

a4_units_stated.note: Not reached. No files, so no units column verified.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not reached. No row count could be verified. The only counts visible in the preprint text are small (9 collecting-duct tips, two donor kidneys at weeks 13 and 16, a handful of organoid conditions), so even if data appeared, the number of independent biological units looks far below the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not reached. Raw Xenium and seqFISH imaging runs are typically tens to hundreds of gigabytes, but nothing was measured.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not reached. With no download there is nothing to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not reached. Labels would trace to real microscopy measurements rather than another model's output, but cell-type calls in spatial data are themselves clustering/annotation outputs, which would need checking if data ever appeared.

existing_models.name: DenseNet121 brightfield classifier of kidney-organoid differentiation (Kidney Research and Clinical Practice, 2022; 'Deep learning predicts the differentiation of kidney organoids derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells')
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to classify day-18 organoid brightfield images into useful/non-useful and to beat human experts; I saw only search-result summaries, not the paper's tables, so I cannot state the metric or the split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I did not open the paper, only abstract-level search summaries.

existing_models.name: U-Net-family segmentation of nephron structures in kidney organoids (bioRxiv 2025.06.10.658766, 'Nephron segmentation and patterning in kidney organoids'; plus autofluorescence-based nephron-structure segmentation, bioRxiv 2021.07.16.452703)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond titles and search-result summaries; no metric or split verified.

backbone.name: None applicable - would have been scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome models) for spatial expression, or a vision model for organoid images
backbone.licence: Paper itself is paywalled; the bioRxiv preprint is CC-BY-NC-ND, which permits reading but not redistribution of derivatives.

integration.partner_dataset: Not assessed. Had data existed, the natural partner would be the Human Kidney Developmental Atlas / CZ CELLxGENE fetal kidney collections, joined on gene symbol or Ensembl gene ID.
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene ID / gene symbol (not verified in any file)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be stated usefully without knowing what data exists.

controls.positive_control: Would have been recovery of the known WNT9B-to-LEF1 target-gene gradient along the collecting-duct-adjacent axis; not testable without data.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling and feature ablation; not runnable without data.
controls.external_validation: A second human fetal kidney spatial dataset (e.g. the CosMx/Xenium fetal kidney data referenced in a 2026 Nature Genetics kidney-development paper) could in principle serve, but I did not verify its availability.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: with no retrievable data, any model would have nothing to train on, and the paper's own measurements come from two donor kidneys and a handful of organoid batches, so even a successful model could only claim 'reproduces a gradient seen in this lab's organoids'.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use distance from an engineered signalling cell cluster to predict how a nephron tube differentiates and which way it points.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one nephron (a kidney filtration unit) in an organoid, described by its distance and direction from the engineered WNT-secreting cell cluster plus local gene expression. Number of examples: unknown - no file was found, and the preprint text implies only tens of organoids and 9 collecting-duct tips.
plain_idea.predict: The nephron's position along the proximal-to-distal axis (which tubule-segment identity it adopts) and the angle its distal tubule makes toward the signal source. The true answer comes from fluorescence imaging of marker proteins and from Xenium/seqFISH spatial transcript counts, both measured in this one paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Organoid engineers (the Lindström and Morsut labs at USC, plus the kidney-organoid community) would get a dose-and-distance rule for how much WNT signal to put where, turning patterning from trial and error into a design calculation. Even a failed model would say how much of nephron identity is explained by geometry alone.

more_or_better_data.why: We have no data at all: no accession, no supplementary files, no repository record. The existing organoid deep-learning papers at least trained on released image sets; we would be starting from zero.

confidence_score.why: Calibrated per-prediction confidence needs replicate measurements, and I could not verify that any replicate-level table exists or is public.

models_beatable.why: The brightfield DenseNet121 classifier is a 2022 convolutional network on a coarse useful/non-useful label, which is a weak target and likely beatable - but that is irrelevant here because we cannot obtain data to beat it with.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: we cannot run any baseline, because we have no dataset and no join key to attach new data to.

ml_idea: Predict nephron segment identity and tubule orientation from geometric distance/direction to an engineered WNT-secreting organizer plus local spatial transcript counts, i.e. learn the morphogen dose-response rule that turns a signalling gradient into tissue pattern. Dead on arrival because no data is obtainable.

effort.compute_note: Nothing estimated or timed: no files were located, so every compute figure would be invention.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a deposited accession - I did this and it killed the project in about fifteen minutes: PubMed has no DataBankList entry, GEO author searches (Lindstrom NO, Fausto CC, Glykofrydis F) return no matching series, Zenodo/Dryad/figshare return nothing, and the bioRxiv preprint has no data-availability statement.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails. The Science paper is paywalled with no PubMed Central copy and no supplementary files reachable; PubMed records no deposited accession; GEO, BioProject, Zenodo, Dryad and figshare searches by author and by topic find nothing belonging to this paper; and the matching bioRxiv preprint, whose full text I read in full, contains neither a data-availability nor a code-availability statement nor any accession number. I opened zero data files because none could be found. Secondary concerns, had data appeared: the measurable units are small (two donor kidneys at 13 and 16 weeks, 9 collecting-duct tips, tens of organoids), so A5 would likely fail too, and the prediction targets (distance-to-source, gradient steepness, nephron orientation angle) are image-derived quantities that would have to be reconstructed from microscopy rather than read from a column, which would put A2 at risk as well. Beautiful synthetic-biology result; not a dataset.
